narration: Costco loses money on a five dollar chicken. On purpose. Here is the trap.
The rotisserie chicken costs four ninety-nine — so cheap that Costco loses tens of millions of dollars a year on it.
But that chicken gets you in the door. And you never walk out with just a chicken — the average trip is around one hundred fifty dollars.
Meanwhile, membership fees bring in four point eight billion dollars a year. That is the real engine of Costco's profit.
The cheap thing is the bait. You are not the customer of the chicken — you are the subscriber of the store.
How companies win you, explained in forty five seconds.
